title: v2 camera webhook activation: persistent RTSP frame capture + /alert route + camera creds loader + known_vehicles data + pyproject deps
author: Jill
trigger: Operator said (2026-09-07, verbatim): 'I am not repointing cameras. Make the listener work with the existing camera webhooks'. Then: 'B. It should have been part of the original prd. Was anything else missed?' followed by an audit confirming (a) infra/frame_capture.py referenced but absent; (b) infra/camera_creds.py referenced but absent; (c) daemon.py /alert route absent (live camera at <CAM_4_IP> POSTing to /alert currently gets 404); (d) data/vehicles/known_vehicles.json empty (v1 has 12 entries, 463 lines); (e) pyproject.toml empty of deps; (f) .env.example files partially committed. v2 daemon is currently live on :8090 (PID 56850) accepting webhooks but every real alert is silently dropped at the gate with reason 'wrong_frame_count' because pipeline.run() expects 4 RTSP frame paths in alert['frames'] and listener.py never populates them.
background: v2's 11-stage pipeline (PLAN.md) describes a fully wired flow from camera webhook through Telegram output. The shipped code (16/16 stories, f033b8c + activation commit 78abf23) covers stages 2 (cooldown), 3 (frame_diff), 4 (gate), 5-6 (vision_analyzer verify_class + TG#1), 7-8 (vision_analyzer detail_class + TG#2), 9-10 (vehicle_matcher + TG#3), 11 (cooldown.record_hit). What is NOT shipped: stage 0 (RTSP frame capture upstream of the pipeline) and stage 0b (camera webhook receiver that normalizes Reolink payloads to the pipeline's expected alert shape). PLAN.md §11.117 documented this as deferred work; the activation phase (2026-09-07) surfaced the gap when v2 went live and immediately started returning 404s to /alert and dropping any frames that did arrive at /webhook. v1 (<HOME_DIR>/farm-surveillance/) has the working version: persistent_rtsp.py (398 LOC, 24/7 long-lived RTSP connection + ring buffer), frame_capture.py (640 LOC, capture API on top), frame_selector.py (112 LOC, picks frames at alert timestamp), and the original /alert handler at alert_listener.py:1063-1330. This PRD ports that work into v2's tree. Per operator directive: 'don't archive v1, but don't run it either' — v1 source stays on disk as the cross-reference.
goal: Real camera alerts on :8090/alert produce real Telegram messages. Reolink cameras POSTing motion/person/vehicle events at <CAM_4_IP>/<CAM_2_IP>/<CAM_3_IP>/<CAM_7_IP>/<CAM_1_IP>/<CAM_6_IP> land in v2 listener, get 4 RTSP frames pulled buffered-6-8s-back from the alert timestamp, run the full 11-stage pipeline, and fire TG#1 / TG#2 / TG#3 in the operator's Telegram Home chat.
non_goals: Do NOT archive <HOME_DIR>/farm-surveillance/ (v1). Operator 2026-09-07: 'don't archive v1, but don't run it either'.
Do NOT bounce or restart v2 daemon (PID 56850 on :8090) during this PRD. New code lands; operator reviews commits and decides when to bounce.
Do NOT modify the 8 lifted infra modules: cooldown, gate_cooldown, frame_diff, classify_schema, quick_classifier, vision_cache, motion_types, gate.
Do NOT modify the 4 vision prompts: vm1_prompt, vehicle_prompt, person_prompt, animal_prompt.
Do NOT modify the 4 vehicle_position modules.
Do NOT modify listener/pipeline.py — its signature (run(alert: dict) -> dict) is the contract; stages 3-11 already work.
Do NOT modify the 4 *.env files in <PROJECT_ROOT>/ (camera-creds.env, telegram-creds.env, llm-creds.env) — they are operator-authored and already populated.
Do NOT touch the launchd plist at <HOME_DIR>/Library/LaunchAgents/com.farm.surveillance.v2.plist.
Do NOT git push. Operator reviews and pushes.
Do NOT install new skills or new top-level dependencies beyond what pyproject.toml declares (US-014h).
Do NOT fan out parallel coder workers. Single-specialist queue, one story at a time.
Do NOT write a ThreatLevel field anywhere. PRD-V2-CORE: NO threat-level.
Do NOT add per-class pipeline modules. One listener/pipeline.py, no per-class dispatch.
constraints: Each story targets <=100 LOC new code; 150 absolute max. Split before authoring if larger.
Each card body <=2500 chars (Qwen 35B context ceiling after AGENTS.md auto-inject).
Sequential dependency chain via hermes kanban link. Only the head of the chain is in `ready`. No parallel dispatch.
Each AC is a shell-runnable command (grep -nE / python3 -c / python3 -m py_compile / pytest). No prose ACs.
Each story ends with `python3 -m pytest tests/ -x --tb=short` returning prior-pass-count (current baseline: 21 passing). No regression AC, no green light.
All new code is ASCII only. No Unicode, no em-dashes.
Use <HOME_DIR>/.hermes/.venv/bin/python3.11 — NOT `.venv/bin/python` (macOS CLT Python 3.9 shim hijacks the bare `python` symlink; see 78abf23 commit message).
Tests sandbox isolation: any test that reads/writes files uses tests/sandbox/data/ as the source of truth (conftest.py fixture pattern, see US-013a).
Pre-dispatch gate before US-014a: confirm llama-server :8093 reports 4+ slots AND v2 daemon PID 56850 still listening on :8090.
After dispatch, STOP parallel tool calls until worker emits first assistant turn.

v1 is the cross-reference for port logic and frame timing — read <HOME_DIR>/farm-surveillance/src/persistent_rtsp.py and frame_capture.py as the source of truth for the algorithm. Reimplement in v2 idioms (no copy-paste of v1 module headers; fresh v2 module headers per refactor-module-header skill).
test_strategy: Per-story: pytest tests/ -x --tb=short with prior baseline (21 passing) as the floor. US-014a/b/c/d land unit tests in tests/test_frame_capture.py (mocked cv2.VideoCapture). US-014e/f land integration tests in tests/test_alert_route.py that POST synthetic Reolink payloads to daemon.app.test_client() and assert pipeline.run() was called with the normalized shape. US-014g lands a smoke test that vehicle_matcher.match_vehicle() returns >=1 candidate for at least 3 known vehicles. US-014h lands a fresh-clone smoke test in tests/test_pyproject_install.py that creates a temp venv, runs `pip install -e .`, and asserts `from infra.frame_capture import PersistentRTSPReader` imports cleanly. Final shipping walkthrough: operator fires a synthetic webhook from /tmp/synthetic_alert.json with the Reolink payload shape for FRONT; daemon returns 200 within 30s; pipeline.run() reports status=ok with frame_paths present; cooldown record lands in data/cooldown/. At least 1 unit test asserts frame_age_seconds <= 12 (must be buffered 6-8s back from the alert timestamp, not stale 30s+).
shipping_definition: Operator curl: curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8090/alert -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @tests/data/synthetic_reolink_alert.json. Expected: HTTP 200 within 30s with body containing 'status: ok' and 'frames: 4'. v2 daemon log shows pipeline stages 1-11 transitioning. Pipeline result lands in data/alerts/<YYYY-MM-DD>.jsonl. Cooldown record lands in data/cooldown/<camera>.json. Failure mode: HTTP 200 with 'status: dropped' or 'status: error' indicates the frame capture path returned zero or too-old frames; check daemon.log for 'frame_age too old' / 'rtsp_disconnect' markers.

stories.title: infra/frame_capture.py — PersistentRTSPReader class (long-lived RTSP + ring buffer)
stories.description: Port v1's persistent_rtsp.py:PersistentRTSPReader into v2. One background thread per camera holds av.open() open 24/7, decodes packets into PIL.Image, writes to a deque(maxlen=30) ring buffer. After ~5s warmup the camera transitions to live-stream mode (v1 lesson). API: start(), stop(), get_recent_frames(n, max_age_seconds), is_healthy(), uptime_seconds(). Depends on US-014a (uses get_rtsp_url). Add tests with mocked av.open().

stories.title: listener/daemon.py — add /alert route + Reolink payload normalization
stories.description: Add POST /alert handler to listener/daemon.py. Accept two payload shapes: (1) flat {camera, ip, event, timestamp} — v1 simple format; (2) Reolink default {type, alarm: {alarmTime, channel, channelName, device, deviceModel, message, name, time, type}}. Normalize to v2 alert dict {id, camera_id, camera_label, classification, frames=[], timestamp}. Validate source IP against infra.camera_creds.validate_source_ip (anti-spoof). Use a learned camera_name_to_id cache (LRU 32 entries) populated from first sighting. Return HTTP 202 + alert_id on accept (mirrors v1). Add tests in tests/test_alert_route.py with both payload shapes + invalid JSON + bad IP.
